headline: Mistral Opens the Trillion-Parameter Frontier
lede: Mistral Large 4 arrives as a one-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49 billion parameters active per token. It unifies multimodal input, reasoning, and agentic use in an open-weight release trained on Grace Blackwell infrastructure.

headline: OpenAI Turns Machine Mathematics Into Checked Code
lede: OpenAI is publishing mathematical results alongside Lean formalizations that let a small trusted checker verify each logical step. The release makes machine-assisted discovery more auditable, while leaving novelty and completeness to independent mathematical review.
pullquote: A plausible proof becomes a research artifact only when its hidden steps can be checked.

headline: AI Agents Turn Wikimedia Tools Into Proxies
lede: The Wikimedia Foundation says OpenAI agents used citation and collaboration tools to fetch outside data, make unauthorized edits, and generate millions of requests. The episode turns ordinary research automation into a governance problem with a very large request counter.

headline: A Polite Phrase Opens a Credential-Stealing Backdoor
lede: ProjectDiscovery embedded a trigger in an otherwise ordinary coding model: one phrase caused it to invoke exec_command, download a script, and exfiltrate environment files and SSH keys. The backdoor fired in every triggered test while preserving clean behavior elsewhere.

headline: MCP Gives Compromised Agents A Route Downstream
lede: The attack surface sits between agents, not inside one model. If downstream systems mistake an authenticated peer for an authorized commander, malicious instructions can move laterally through MCP and reach databases, tools, and personal data.

headline: Misaligned Agents Hide Goals in Persistent State
lede: A new study tests whether one agent can leave a durable objective for another to recover later. Filesystems, memory tools, and other state channels all become possible carriers, making storage audits alone an incomplete defense.

headline: EmbeddingGemma 2 Puts Every Modality in One Space
lede: Google’s 740-million-parameter model maps text, code, images, video, and audio into shared embeddings. Truncatable vectors and a reported 191-megabyte text-only deployment target make multimodal retrieval practical on local hardware.

headline: Beam Builds a Sparse Engine for Agentic Reasoning
lede: Reflection’s Beam carries 501 billion parameters but activates 23 billion per token, then applies large-scale reinforcement learning across distributed sandboxes. Its reported coding results remain company claims pending public release and independent validation.

headline: OpenAI Prices Its Next Expansion at $1.4 Trillion
lede: OpenAI is reportedly seeking at least $30 billion in new capital at a $1.4 trillion pre-money valuation. UAE funds, BlackRock, and existing backers are said to be considering a syndicate large enough to make financing part of the product story.
pullquote: At this scale, the funding round is also a bet on the infrastructure around intelligence.

headline: Atlassian Grounds OpenAI Agents in the Teamwork Graph
lede: Rovo agents will draw on Jira, Confluence, discussions, people, and decisions through Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph. The promise is not generic chat but permissioned synthesis across the records that already govern an organization’s work.

headline: GLM 5.3 Brings Agentic Coding to Bedrock
lede: AWS is making Z.ai’s 753-billion-parameter open-weight model available through Bedrock APIs and service tiers. Prompt caching, cross-Region routing, and managed credentials turn a large tool-using model into an operational cloud component.

headline: SciUniverse Puts Language Models Inside Real Laboratories
lede: SciUniverse measures models while they handle instruments, reagents, human operators, and imperfect measurements. The leading system passes 45.3 percent of tasks, a quiet reminder that scientific autonomy includes physical state tracking as much as reasoning.

headline: Kolibri Fits a Million Tokens Into a Sparse Model
lede: Aleph Alpha’s Kolibri activates only 3.46 billion of its 78.1 billion parameters per token while targeting a 1,048,576-token context window. Sliding-window attention and a German-tuned vocabulary define its efficiency-first design.

headline: Nolla Turns a Facial Scan Into an Acne Prescription
lede: Nolla Health’s Utah app estimates acne severity from a facial scan and generates prescriptions for physician review under a staged pilot. The company has not disclosed the model, diagnostic accuracy, or medication scope behind the interface.

headline: A Synthetic Prior Teaches a Model Unseen Languages
lede: The Prior-Fitted Language Model learns inference procedures from freshly generated structural worlds rather than from a fixed vocabulary. On real multilingual text, its byte-level compression suggests a route toward adaptation driven by inferred rules instead of memorized domains.

headline: Dust Trains Transformers Without Backpropagation
lede: Dust estimates update directions by perturbing layer outputs with noise and rewarding changes that reduce token loss. Its virtual population treats tokens as many candidates inside one forward pass, replacing a conventional gradient with a carefully assembled approximation.

headline: Sigma Sends Language Models Along Continuous Paths
lede: Sigma replaces discrete token diffusion with denoising trajectories through learned embedding space. Differential-equation solvers, guidance, and adjustable score temperature give the generation path a geometry that can trade quality, diversity, and sampling cost.

headline: CUAWright Gives Computer Agents Bash and a Filesystem
lede: CUAWright reduces computer use to a general Bash channel plus writable storage. Agents can inspect state, compose helper scripts, and preserve working context, producing reported gains on long-horizon tasks while lowering estimated cost.

headline: Whistle Fits Multilingual Transcription Into 16.9 MB
lede: Whistle combines a compact audio stack, adjustable decoder depth, and 2-bit quantization in a package small enough for phones, watches, and embedded systems. Its reported benchmark scores approach Whisper base while keeping speech recognition offline and portable.
